# the contributor audit: sharp dimensional tails and the four-triangle peak closure

## Sharp dimensional weighted tails: PASS

I read `candidate bb74919333cc624f` in full and
ran `supporting computation verify_sharp_dimensional_weighted_three_tails.py`. All displayed
coefficient vectors, 505 rational frustum identities, the large-d
rational comparison, and simplex/subset equality arithmetic pass.

I independently derived the sharp coefficient from the untruncated
decreasing cone: minimizing (a-s)^d/[1-(a+s)^d], a=d/(d+1), gives
v=a+s=(2a)^(-1/(d-1)), and the ratio is exactly the displayed lambda_d.
The cut levels are proper, s is positive, and the equality subset is
an actual convex cap. Thus the coefficient's sharpness is geometric,
not a numerical minimum.

The AM-GM bound lambda<=4Gamma^2 implies both lambda<1 for d>=2 and
lambda<=Gamma/(1-Gamma). These give the zero-shift inequality and the
reduction of negative shifts. The d=1 uniform interval is separate and
has exact coefficient1. The mean-zero localization uses the already
audited negative central-threshold regularization; its admissible Diracs
have objective at most1. No atom at zero receives an untracked CDF term.

The powered truncated-mean concavity follows from the stated exact
second derivative and Cauchy--Schwarz. Both endpoints and the direction
of its chord inequality are correct. In the decreasing orientation,
the critical branch starts at a zero numerator and ends at a
nonnegative numerator; concavity fills its entire valid interval.
The constant branch is paid by the ordinary centroid inequality.

The increasing orientation has its minimum exactly when the upper cut
reaches the support endpoint. The polynomial identity for its deficit
has positive denominator, and all finite-dimensional coefficient
certificates are explicitly printed in the proof. Positive Bernstein
basis functions (or positive monomials for d=6) supply exact sign
certificates. The computation supplements an inspectable finite
algebraic proof rather than replacing an all-profile argument.

For d>=7, I reread the referenced quadrature proof in
`candidate 732b11a769399016`, Sections5--6.
Its logarithmic derivative has only the asserted possible minima;
the four-term rational logarithm bound certifies the interior one.
The positive Stieltjes representation integrates finite nonnegative
comparisons, yielding T<=1/6. Together with monotonic Gamma and the
exact positive rational d=7 gap, this treats every remaining dimension.

The subset payment optimizes the exact bound max(0,a-V+F(t)) at its
single kink; signs on both sides follow from0<lambda<=1. It retains
one common normal and opposite shifts. Its sharpness uses a convex
subset, and all continuous boundaries are measure-null. No repeated
use of the middle term or assertion about arbitrary mixed sources
is part of the theorem.

## Elementary triangle coefficient7/9: PASS

I separately read `candidate 6c259b3f68b388b0`
and ran its symbolic verifier. All ten threshold cells, their endpoint
and stationary signs, both full Bernstein certificates, 717 rational
extremum checks, and the actual sharp source cap pass. Repeated vertex
heights are obtained by continuous limits with nonzero scalar normals.
This supplies a separate elementary triangle proof, consistent with
the all-body dimensional theorem.

## Four-triangle peak theorem and translation corollary: PASS

I read `candidate 86b03c88b3643f55`,
including Section7, and ran its verifier: all scalar identities, 2200
radius profiles, 3520 actual-normal/all-tilt checks, and closed vertical
caps pass. I independently obtained the decisive e=1/4 split and both
completed squares before the proof was completed.

The first shear sends the retained middle and right fibers to bK and K;
the transformed small fiber lies in (2b-1)K, hence in bK. The second
shear gives the exact intersection hT-sg after the common translation.
Its middle-volume correction uses homothetic bodies with the SAME
centroid. All omitted source portions add nonnegative cap mass, and
vertical caps are checked separately. Both proposed centers are actual
own-fiber centroids after pulling back the permitted shears.

The scalar alternatives exhaust c>=b and c<=b, and h=0 is separate.
All endpoint signs of the concave quadratics have the stated exact
values. Selecting the first centroid only when its proved lower bound
meets the target, and the second otherwise, gives one deterministic
center. Combining with the independently audited monotone theorem
exhausts every positive concave four-radius sequence.

I also reread `candidate 24467ade6f021ae8`.
Its fixed common-vertex simplex comparison dominates EACH corresponding
actual own-centroid depth, for arbitrary compatible translations. The
four positive bases are consecutive and their radii are concave by
Brunn--Minkowski. Thus Section7 legitimately transfers the four-fiber
result to arbitrary compatibly translated homothetic triangles, and
zero-area extra fibers change no measured mass. It does not extend
to arbitrary numbers of positive fibers or nonhomothetic shapes.
note: Mathematical discussion retained to expose corrections and limitations. This is not a verification run, accepted premise, or approval of the revised submission. Association follows explicit source-document references, not an inferred dependency.
